difficultyRationale: Requires separating reflective openness from compile-time export accessibility at module granularity.
prompt: Which statements about an `open module` declaration are correct? Select all that apply.
explanation: An open module opens all of its packages for deep reflective access by other modules. Openness is not the same as exporting packages for ordinary compile-time access.

options.text: All packages in the module are open for deep reflection.
options.explanation: That is the defining effect of declaring the whole module open.

options.text: Every package is automatically exported for ordinary source-level access.
options.explanation: Opening and exporting are separate JPMS concepts.

options.text: The module can still use exports directives to control ordinary API access.
options.explanation: An open module may still export selected packages while all packages remain open reflectively.

options.text: An open module becomes an unnamed module.
options.explanation: It remains a named module; `open` changes reflective accessibility.
